doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Century, Alabama: a wild town
summary: Billie describes Century as a wild town with gambling, moonshine, dancing and houses with piano.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Let's see, we got interrupted there, Mr. Brooks, the insurance man, came in and we recorded a little of his views on music. We were talking about Alabama.
Yeah, we were talking about Alabama.
Up there around Atmore. Atmore, Molina. And that was a tough town, you were saying, what's the name of that town, Paul?

Century, that's old heck yeah, Century was a wild town, whoa, yes indeed. It used to be a wild, I'm telling you. It got a little tame now, ain't like it used to be. It's a little civilized now, but it was a wild town.
So what went on in a wild town?
You just had to be wild with them, that's all. What come you just had to go along with them?

Gambling, yes. Gambling, moonshine liquor, dancing, with them jokes, understand? Jokes, they would call them jokes up in the inbox. Jokes. You know what the hell, just have piano, that's all, anybody can play on the piano, just play on the piano.
Piano and drum, either one, something like that.
And plenty to eat, call them children struts, you know, children.
Those houses up there I guess with the girls and everything, you know?
